newsitem.title: GERMANY: German railways let homeless sleep in stations.
newsitem.headline: German railways let homeless sleep in stations.

text.p: Germany's national railway company said on Saturday it was letting the homeless spend the night in railway stations to shelter from the severe cold, which has claimed over 30 lives.
A spokesman for Deutsche Bahn AG said the stations were still being locked at night, but homeless people were not being thrown out as usual.
The city of Frankfurt also agreed to keep two underground railway stations open at night for the homeless.
More than 30 people, many of them sleeping rough, have died in Germany in the cold snap, when night-time temperatures have dipped below minuis 26 degrees Celsius (minus 15F).

Around 5,000 tourists were forced to extend their stay on the East Friesian holiday islands of Spiekeroog, Wangerooge and Juist as ice in the North Sea up to 30 cm thick prevented ferries shuttling to the mainland.
Island authorities said they hoped most of the tourists would have been able to leave on small aircraft by Monday.
